behaviours.verdictNote: dropped at the v3.16.0 merge: upstream replaced ajv with jsonschema themselves, so form.tsx and options-schema.ts are now byte-identical to upstream, and the fork's own jsonschema dependency, a duplicate of upstream's, is gone. The fork also carried native-url plus a resolve.alias key in packages/ketcher-react/rollup.config.ts; resolve is not a RollupOptions key, so that alias never took effect, and both were removed with the rest. Reapply this behaviour if upstream ever returns to ajv: main serves the platform under a CSP whose script-src carries no 'unsafe-eval' (main/site/unc_flask/csp.txt; the only exemption is the CAD wasm worker), and ajv validates by compiling schemas with new Function (ajv/dist/compile/index.js), which that CSP blocks, so every ketcher dialog that validates a form would fail in the platform. jsonschema interprets instead and needs no codegen. The fork demo page is not served under main's CSP, so an upstream ajv would pass every fork test and break only main. ketcher-core's own ajv dependency is unaffected: its prebuild script precompiles the KET schema, so no codegen runs in the browser.

behaviours.summary: Guard the lookups vanilla dereferences unchecked when an operation is replayed against a structure that no longer holds the atom, half bond or editor it names.
behaviours.verdictNote: reapply, and note a second file the coverage check cannot see: v3.18.0 added upstream's own __tests__/application/editor/actions/isDummy.test.ts, which asserts AtomAttr.isDummy returns false when the atom is gone. This fork asserts true, so the action drops the operation. Upstream guarded only isDummy and left execute doing atoms.get(aid)!, so their false makes the action keep an operation that then dereferences the missing atom, which is the crash this behaviour exists to prevent. The AtomAttr assertion in that upstream test is changed to true and carries a comment saying why; expect it to conflict on later merges. The manifest claims packages/*/src only, so nothing else will flag it.

behaviours.summary: Keep text nodes serializing data.pos, and do not crash on a text node with fewer points than a bounding box needs.
behaviours.verdictNote: two deltas in one file, both added at the v3.18.0 merge. Upstream rewrote text serialization for lexical: it now writes geometry as boundingBox and drops data.pos, and it builds that box from pos[0], pos[1] and pos[2] before its own legacy-format check. First, a text node saved by an earlier ketcher can carry only two points, so pos[2].x threw and an existing structure with such text could not be serialized at all. Second, main reads text geometry from data.pos in three places: reaction diagram bounds in ketcher_layout.py, _extract_text_reagents in build_reaction_diagram_from_chem_struct.py, which drops a reagent whose coordinates are missing, and calculate_chemical_reaction_combiner.py. Writing only boundingBox loses text reagents from reaction diagrams with no error. This fork writes data.pos alongside upstream's boundingBox so the backend contract is unchanged. Expect a conflict here on every merge, since upstream is actively changing this file; the alternative is teaching those three consumers to read boundingBox, at which point this delta can go.
